title: Generative causal mediation vs. plain CAA: which gives a cleaner safety steering vector?

original_idea.body: Compare CAA and generative-causal-mediation steering vectors at matched effect, measuring collateral damage on unrelated capability benchmarks.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Cleaner safety steering reduces collateral capability damage, but the chain to catastrophic-risk reduction is moderate/indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Two steering methods at matched effect + capability benchmarks; the causal-mediation variant adds complexity; intermediate-guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused head-to-head but requires implementing the causal-mediation method plus matched-effect calibration.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public model/benchmarks, no internal access; method comparison is externally doable, lab-deprioritized.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only on one model + small benchmark subsets; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Both methods are published; the head-to-head side-effect comparison is a partly-open application.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Both steering methods are published; the head-to-head collateral-damage comparison may be a partly-open application.
